programs.title: Ship Vue AI chat with API-owned runtime state and websocket analytics
programs.objective: Implement the founder-required cross-repo AI workspace as a real Vue SPA general LLM chat agent, not a narrow recurring-quotes slice and not a bootstrap-only or compatibility-envelope deliverable. Prioritize the AI side of the Vue AI workspace and end-to-end capability first. API must give Vue the websocket URL it should use for the agent runtime. In local development, that websocket target must route through the t3code-vxapp pathway. In live environments, the websocket/backend shape must support an API endpoint that can be proxied through nginx. All agent runtime state for Vue requests must be owned by api-vxapp. This includes new OOP CRUD services for threads, chat history, skills, workspace/runtime config, and the runtime/config entities required by the AI workspace. This is not satisfied by only returning bootstrap metadata. Vue must handle websockets for analytics as well. api-vxapp must expose another websocket-capable service for deep page tracking and monitoring so the agent can observe real-time and historical user interaction context. Minimum analytics/tracking coverage includes: current movements; previous movements; mouse location; current page; previous pages; previous time on pages; hovering over components; clicked tooltips; focused an input then moved away; opened recent drawers and dialogs; suddenly exited drawers and dialogs; previous API request log; likely validation errors the user has been having; everything else reasonably required to let the agent understand current user behavior in context. The list above is a minimum requirement and must not be paraphrased downward. api-vxapp must create several new OOP CRUD services for this work. Move/refactor the current session implementation out of Kernal into a top-level Vortex\Sessions surface with subservices for tracking/runtime metadata this feature needs. Significant refactoring is expected and in scope. Reuse dynamic workspace generation and workspace packs. Configuration authority for that workspace must come from api-vxapp. Vue must have CRUD to change workspace packs, add skills, update skills, create skills, and otherwise manage workspace configuration needed for full AI functionality. This likely requires changes in agents-vxapp as well as api-vxapp, vue-vxapp, and t3code-vxapp. All Vue-side agents must be workspace-scoped only. No full system permissions. No full system access. Repo execution scope: vue-vxapp must implement the real AI workspace UI and runtime consumer path, consume API bootstrap/session/runtime data, support websocket chat, support analytics websocket integration, support CRUD UI flows for packs, skills, and workspace config required for the AI workspace, and must not ship a fake shell. api-vxapp must own runtime persistence and runtime config authority, implement real service surfaces and not just envelope fields, create/refactor into proper OOP CRUD services, create the Vortex\Sessions top-level surface and move/refactor current session implementation out of Kernal, add persistence and APIs for runtime session state, threads, chat history, skills, workspace config, and required analytics/tracking data, and provide websocket bootstrap data plus the real supporting backend behind it. t3code-vxapp must provide the local websocket pathway used by the API-provided websocket URL in development and ensure the local routing path is actually usable by the AI workspace flow. agents-vxapp must be included wherever dynamic workspace generation, workspace packs, or workspace-scoped permission contracts require source changes. What does not count as success: a websocket URL field alone; a session/bootstrap envelope alone; a compatibility wrapper alone; a Vue shell without runtime/config/analytics backend; or any claim of completion while the implementation is still only bootstrap/session metadata or placeholder runtime wiring. API-vxapp detailed requirements are locked in Program metadata_json.apiVxappRequirements and are part of this Program contract, including Vortex\\Sessions namespace structure, expanded telemetry capture, runtime config authority, OOP CRUD service families, and Vue -> API -> t3 -> API -> Vue websocket flow. Exact API websocket integration plan is locked in Program metadata_json.apiVxappRequirements.exactWebsocketIntegrationPlan. runtime-gateway-vxapp is a required Rust microservice for browser-facing websocket/runtime gateway ownership and live websocket session tracking. runtime-gateway-vxapp setup/bootstrap is part of Program 99: scaffold the Rust service from the local blank clone at /home/gizmo/runtime-gateway-vxapp, and after the agents-vxapp refactor is audited, register it under the current agent-runtime/repos pattern with worker manifests/skills so agents can dispatch to it. Vue-vxapp detailed requirements are locked in Program metadata_json.vueVxappRequirements and are part of this Program contract: global assistant panel first, replace the legacy REST AI modal/FAB with the API/runtime-gateway-backed assistant, capture whole-app analytics, provide streaming tool-capable chat, ship a full API-backed thread sidebar, and provide full runtime config CRUD UI for packs, skills, agents, workspace config, revisions, publish/rollback/archive, and effective config display. Shared cross-repo contract pipeline requirements are locked in Program metadata_json.crossRepoContractPipeline: stores-vxapp owns generator tooling and @Contracts/Runtime distribution, api-vxapp and agents-vxapp each emit a common JSON contract IR from their own source-authority contracts, generated TypeScript/Rust/PHP-helper outputs are distributed through stores-vxapp, and runtime-gateway-vxapp must consume stores-vxapp as a required submodule for generated Rust contracts. Cross-repo certainty is now explicit: stores-vxapp distributes generated runtime contracts including Rust output; agents-vxapp owns agent-facing contracts and worker dispatch context; t3code-vxapp is local relay only; shared runtime protocol and phased implementation order are part of Program 99 acceptance. Founder decisions persisted: slave-vxapp is compatibility-only for this Program; t3code consumes stores-vxapp as a submodule; runtime-gateway requires Docker and comprehensive E2E before PR readiness; analytics is default enabled; Control websocket is in first build; retention/redaction follows performance-and-security best practices; live provider execution is owned by Rust ai-provider-vxapp rather than t3code-vxapp or agents-vxapp. Founder decision persisted: live provider/model execution will be a dedicated Rust microservice from day 1; ai-provider-vxapp now exists as a blank local clone at /home/gizmo/ai-provider-vxapp; api-vxapp remains durable authority and runtime-gateway-vxapp remains browser websocket owner. New service repos are now created and locally cloned: runtime-gateway-vxapp at /home/gizmo/runtime-gateway-vxapp and ai-provider-vxapp at /home/gizmo/ai-provider-vxapp; both are blank and still need agent-runtime registration plus scaffolding. Agent-runtime registration for runtime-gateway-vxapp and ai-provider-vxapp is intentionally deferred until agents-vxapp refactor state is audited and the existing registration pattern can be followed; ai-provider-vxapp is Rust. Implementation determinations now cover all non-API-namespace unknowns: Rust service baselines, typed contract generation through stores-vxapp, t3/vue consumers, agent-runtime registration pattern, strict validation, TDD, and Docker/Playwright E2E.
